title: Q-STD-cloudevents: write every ledger row between loops as a CloudEvents 1.0 envelope
body:
**Owner:** executor
**Trigger:** executor tick, driver order
**Done check:** cmd:python3 -m foundation standards --adopted cloudevents
**Status:** closed

New handoff events (audit chain data), new provenance rows (ops/provenance.jsonl) and outbound webhooks are CloudEvents 1.0 envelopes built by seed/worker/src/cloudevents.js and foundation/cloudevents.py (shared vectors: seed/standards/cloudevents-vectors.json). Still in their own row shapes: the other ops/*.jsonl ledgers written through foundation/ledger.py `append`, D1 `handoff_events` as served by /api/v1/handoffs (site/controlplane.js), the dashboard's provenance table and the body of POST /api/fleet/provenance (dashboard/worker.js, foundation/provenance.py `push`). For each: wrap on write with type io.ultrastable.<area>.<event>, keep readers on `unwrap` so rows written before stay readable, never rewrite history. Serve /api/v1/handoffs events with content type application/cloudevents-batch+json when the caller asks for it. Add each path's test beside the existing ones.

STANDARDS-FIRST-1 (Rowan, 2026-11-25): "Standards, don't reinvent the wheel. Apply standards." The row is `cloudevents` in seed/standards/standards.json; this item closes when that row reads `"adoption": "adopted"` and every probe on it passes. Change the row in the same change that makes it true, never before.

**Closing probe:** cmd:python3 -m foundation standards --adopted cloudevents

**Prediction:** spec_quality >= 0.7 within 336 h (read by `python3 -m foundation specgate --report`; this item closing by its done check keeps the share of well-specified open items at or above today's reading)

**Out of scope:** rewriting working internals to carry the label, or changing the row to adopted without code and a probe.

**Disposition:** shelved (ttl, 2026-11-26T05:33:04Z, DISPOSE-1)

**Evidence:** open 6.1 hours (limit 6 hours) and no loop closed it (SLA-8H-1). Its closing probe still runs on every fleet pass and records `fixed` when it passes; the executor retries it when its open queue is empty (every 30 days at most).
